source.place: HTT Proposition 3.2.2.11, proof, final-fiber factorization and extension f_0 (printed pp. 184–185); Proposition 3.1.2.3 for the marked pushout product. No Stacks tag states this simplicial result.

proof.text: First obtain the final-vertex inclusion $e:\{n\}^\sharp\hookrightarrow(\Delta^n)^\sharp$ as marked anodyne. The initial-vertex assertion of [lem-coef-infinity-marked-initial-vertex] gives $\{0\}^\sharp\hookrightarrow(\Delta^n)^\sharp$ marked coanodyne. Apply the order-reversal operation on simplicial sets: the simplex operator $\alpha:[a]\to[b]$ becomes the monotone operator $i\mapsto b-\alpha(a-i)$. It is an involution, preserves degreewise pushouts, transfinite colimits and retract diagrams, preserves full markings, and takes vertex $0$ to vertex $n$. By the explicit reversal identification in [def-coef-infinity-marked-coanodyne], it takes the coanodyne class to the marked-anodyne class. This gives $e$, including $n=0$, when it is the identity.

source.place: Proposition 3.2.2.11, proof, smash-product inclusion; Definition 3.1.1.1 and its order-dual (Remark 3.1.1.2).

proof.text: Form the marked pushout $U=(A^\flat\times(\Delta^n)^\sharp)\amalg_{A^\flat\times\{n\}^\sharp}(A_n^\flat\times\{n\}^\sharp)$. Since $j$ is degreewise injective, its underlying simplicial set is the union of these two subsets of $A_n\times\Delta^n$; in each degree their intersection is exactly $A\times\{n\}$. Give the second piece the map $h$ followed by the inclusion $Y_n\hookrightarrow Y$. It is a marked map because the marked edges of $A_n^\flat\times\{n\}^\sharp$ are degenerate, and simplicial maps preserve degeneracies. Its restriction to the intersection equals that of $s$, by the assumed equality $hj=s|_{A\times\{n\}}$. Hence the two maps glue degreewise to a marked map $u:U\to Y^\natural$. The marking on the pushout is generated by the images of the two piece markings, so $u$ preserves every marked edge. Both piece maps have base coordinate the projection to $\Delta^n$, and therefore $pu$ is the restricted projection.

source.place: Proposition 3.2.2.11, proof, prescribed map on the smash-product source (printed pp. 184–185); degreewise pushout and product markings written out.

proof.text: The inclusion $k:U\hookrightarrow A_n^\flat\times(\Delta^n)^\sharp$ is exactly the pushout product of the degreewise injective marked map $j^\flat:A^\flat\to A_n^\flat$ and the marked-anodyne map $e$ from Step 1, after exchanging the two product factors. The pushout-product assertion of [lem-coef-marked-anodyne-lifting-calculus] therefore makes $k$ marked anodyne. This uses only monicity of $j$; no fibration property of $h$ is needed for this extension step.

source.place: Proposition 3.1.2.3 and its application in Proposition 3.2.2.11, proof, smash-product inclusion (printed pp. 184–185).

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-relative-marked-anodyne-calculus] to the cartesian fibration $p:Y\to\Delta^n$. It gives the right lifting property of $Y^\natural\to(\Delta^n)^\sharp$ against $k$. Use the square whose top map is $u$ and whose bottom map is the projection $A_n^\flat\times(\Delta^n)^\sharp\to(\Delta^n)^\sharp$; it commutes by Step 2. A diagonal is a marked map $\widetilde s$ over $\Delta^n$. Its equality with $u$ on each pushout piece gives respectively $\widetilde s\circ(j\times1)=s$ and $\widetilde s|_{A_n\times\{n\}}=h$, as required. For $n=0$ the second piece is the whole target, so this diagonal is simply $h$. Empty $A$, $A_n$ or final fibers cause no extra nonemptiness requirement in the same square.

title: Marked Cartesian mapping-simplex prism extension
statement: Use small simplicial sets and standard simplices as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], cartesian fibrations and natural markings as in [lem-coef-relative-marked-anodyne-calculus], minimal and full markings as in [lem-coef-marked-anodyne-lifting-calculus], and the Kan model structure of [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper]. Let $n\geq0$, let $p:Y\to\Delta^n$ be a small cartesian fibration, put $Y_n=p^{-1}(n)$, and let $s:A^\flat\times(\Delta^n)^\sharp\to Y^\natural$ be a marked map over $\Delta^n$. Suppose its final-fiber map has a factorization $A\xrightarrow{j}A_n\xrightarrow{h}Y_n$, with $j$ a monomorphism and $h$ a trivial Kan fibration. There is a marked map $\widetilde s:A_n^\flat\times(\Delta^n)^\sharp\to Y^\natural$ over $\Delta^n$ satisfying $\widetilde s\circ(j\times1)=s$ and $\widetilde s|_{A_n\times\{n\}}=h$.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q46-37090446f (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the whole item and all six cited statements, and the statement is true. It also agrees with how the parent lem-coef-cartesian-base-equivalence-invariance uses it in Step 11 (factor as monomorphism then trivial Kan fibration h; build the prism on A_n, equal to h at the final vertex). The statement is unchanged and not weakened. Step 1: {n}^sharp into (Delta^n)^sharp is marked anodyne. It comes from the statement of lem-coef-infinity-marked-initial-vertex ({0}^sharp coanodyne for all n>=0) plus the explicit reversal identification in def-coef-infinity-marked-coanodyne. I matched the generators one by one: inner horns to inner horns; Lambda_0^n with {01} marked to Lambda_n^n with the final edge marked; the Delta^2 generator (iii) maps to itself; Kan complexes stay Kan under op. Step 2 is an elementary gluing: since j is mono, A x Delta^n and A_n x {n} meet exactly in A x {n}, where hj = s. Marked edges of A_n^flat x {n}^sharp are degenerate, hence cartesian. Step 3: k is the pushout product of j^flat and e with the factors swapped, so the pushout-product clause of lem-coef-marked-anodyne-lifting-calculus applies. Step 4: lem-coef-relative-marked-anodyne-calculus gives Y^natural -> (Delta^n)^sharp the right lifting property against marked-anodyne maps for any small base, and restricting the diagonal gives both strict equalities. Edge cases checked: n=0 (k = id, the lift is h), n=1, and A, A_n or Y_n empty. There is no cycle (the closure of 504 nodes does not contain the item). Every cited statement is in the item's own unit, sk-prop-sf-biduality-general; the def-cbc node is a definition, so no tool_uses.
